theme: The kings of north and south; the resurrection of the dead
readingInstruction: Read Daniel 11:1-12:13. This is a long and detailed prophecy of the conflicts between kings of the north and south. Do not get lost in the details. Read for the ending in chapter 12: the resurrection of the dead, and the final word to Daniel.
settingTheScene: This last vision comes in 536 BC, and it traces the history of the Persian and Greek empires, and especially the conflicts between the Ptolemies of Egypt (the king of the south) and the Seleucids of Syria (the king of the north). It culminates in the persecution of the Jewish people under Antiochus Epiphanes in the second century BC, and looks beyond to the end times. Chapter 12 gives the clearest statement of resurrection in the Old Testament.
observation: “But the people who know their God shall stand firm and take action” (11:32).
“And those who are wise among the people shall make many understand, though for some days they shall stumble by sword and flame” (11:33).
“At that time shall arise Michael, the great prince who has charge of your people” (12:1).

“And there shall be a time of trouble, such as never has been since there was a nation till that time. But at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone whose name shall be found written in the book” (12:1).
“And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt” (12:2).
“And those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the sky above; and those who turn many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever” (12:3).
“But you, go your way till the end. And you shall rest and shall stand in your allotted place at the end of the days” (12:13).
“Shut up the words and seal the book, until the time of the end” (12:4).
interpretation:
Chapter 11 is a long survey of history in prophecy, with such detail that critics have claimed it must have been written after the events. Believers see in it the sovereign foreknowledge of God. The point is that history is not random. The kings of the north and south rise and fall, make treaties and break them, and God is working through it. The history culminates in the desecration of the temple by a contemptuous king, and then the picture moves beyond him.

In the midst of the persecution, there is a counterpoint. “The people who know their God shall stand firm and take action.” This is the verse of the chapter. Persecution does not destroy those who know their God. They shall stand firm. And those who are wise will make many understand, even though they stumble by sword and flame. The suffering of the saints is not meaningless: it refines and purifies.

Chapter 12 turns to the end. A time of trouble will come, unlike any before. But Daniel’s people will be delivered, “everyone whose name shall be found written in the book.” Then comes the resurrection promise: “Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.” This is one of the clearest teachings of the resurrection of the dead in the Old Testament. Both the righteous and the wicked will rise. The wise will shine like the stars.

The book ends with a personal word to Daniel. He is told to seal the book until the time of the end, and then, tenderly: “But you, go your way till the end. And you shall rest and shall stand in your allotted place at the end of the days.” The old prophet will rest and rise. It is a fitting close to the long unit of exile. After everything, the final word is of rest and resurrection.
connection: John 5:28-29 says that all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, “those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.” 1 Corinthians 15:51-58 speaks of the resurrection. Matthew 24:21 echoes the “time of trouble such as never has been.” Philippians 2:15 says believers shine like stars in the world. Revelation 20:12-15 mentions the book of life. 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18 comforts us with the hope of resurrection.
application:
Memorize Daniel 11:32b: “The people who know their God shall stand firm and take action.” Ask how your knowledge of God can lead to firm action.

Take comfort in the promise of resurrection when you grieve.

Seek to be one who “turns many to righteousness.” Ask whom God may be calling you to encourage in the faith.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to help you know him and stand firm.
Thank him that your name is written in his book.
Thank him for the hope of the resurrection.
